title: A VOW OR A FREEWILL OFFERING

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If, however, their offering is the result of a vow or is a freewill offering, the sacrifice shall be eaten on the day they offer it, but anything left over may be eaten on the next day.'" - Lev 7:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two other reasons for bringing a fellowship offering: a vow fulfilled, or simply a freewill gift.

The vow offering was the fulfilment of a promise — "Lord, if You bring me through this, I will bring You an offering." God expected such promises to be kept. When you make a vow to God, do not delay to fulfil it (Eccl 5:4). Many people make promises to God in a crisis and forget them once the crisis passes.

The freewill offering had no obligation attached at all. Nobody required it. No promise prompted it. The worshipper simply wanted to give.

That second category is a lovely thing. It means Israel's worship had room for spontaneous, uncommanded love — worship that arose because someone felt like giving, not because a rule demanded it.

Mary of Bethany brought a freewill offering when she broke open expensive perfume over Jesus. Nobody asked her to. Some in the room called it waste. Jesus said, She has done a beautiful thing to me (Mk 14:6).

Not everything in the Christian life should be duty. Some of it should be delight.

When did you last give God something simply because you wanted to?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I made a promise to God that I never kept?
2. When did I last do something for God purely out of love, with nothing requiring it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me keep the promises I make to You, and give me a heart that also gives freely, simply because I love You. Amen.
